{'subtask': "Search the web and scholarly databases (Google Scholar, JSTOR, publisher sites, open-access repositories) to identify candidate articles published between 1988 and 1998 that match this description: an article about African politics/development that draws upon evidence to uphold the notion that tracing a select set of unique historical courses is possible by examining the shifting patterns of political growth across African nations. The phrasing implies analysis of trajectories/paths of political change/regime transitions across African countries.\n\nSteps:\n1) Use keywords combining 'Africa', 'political change', 'political growth', 'trajectories', 'paths', 'historical courses', 'patterns', 'regime transitions', and time filter 1988–1998 inclusive. Consider prominent authors like Michael Bratton, Nicolas van de Walle, Robert H. Bates, Crawford Young, Jeffrey Herbst, Richard Joseph, Goran Hyden, etc. Identify at least 3 plausible candidate articles and provide bibliographic details (author(s), title, journal, year), links/DOIs, and a brief summary of why each fits the description.\n2) For each candidate article, access the full text or a preview and extract the reference list or key citations. Identify cited works whose authors later (between 1992–2001 inclusive) wrote an article arguing that the global spread of democracy would not necessarily bring more stability. Examples to watch for include Jack Snyder (e.g., democratization can increase conflict), Edward Mansfield, Fareed Zakaria (illiberal democracy), Samuel P. Huntington (order vs democracy stability), etc. Do not assume; verify actual titles/abstracts/quotes that support the 'democracy spread ≠ stability' claim.\n3) For each candidate match from step 2, document: the cited work details (title, author, year) found in the African article’s references, and the later cautionary article (title, author, year, journal) within 1992–2001, with a brief description of its argument and links/DOIs.\n4) Present a structured report listing all candidate African articles, their key references, and which cited author(s) match the democracy-stability caution criteria. Include direct quotes or paraphrases from sources where possible. Note any uncertainties (e.g., paywalled references, ambiguous phrasing) and provide alternative plausible interpretations if relevant.\n\nDeliver a processed summary with evidence links and clear reasoning for each candidate chain from African article → cited author → later cautionary article. Avoid overly broad speculation; focus on concrete, verifiable items."} Please provide the answer and detailed supporting information of the subtask given to you.

Then, from that reference list, identify which cited authors published (between 1992–2001 inclusive) articles or essays explicitly arguing that the global spread of democracy would not necessarily bring stability (e.g., warning about instability, conflict, or fragile outcomes during democratization). For each matching author, list:\n- The specific referenced work (as it appears in the 1994 article’s references) with full details.\n- The later cautionary article (1992–2001): title, year, journal or venue, DOI/link, and a one-sentence summary of the argument.\n- Indicate clearly whether Jack Snyder appears anywhere in the 1994 reference list; if not, state that he is not a cited author in that article and should not be included in the chain.\nOutput a structured report with source links (DOIs, JSTOR, publisher pages) and note any uncertainties due to paywalls or incomplete reference exports.
